title: Experiment: multi-year on-prem subscription with staged upgrade lanes and SQ template
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Purpose: run a structured experiment to validate a multi-year on-prem / VPC subscription product that pairs a license fee + ops credits model with staged upgrade lanes (standard quarterly, opt-in monthly, emergency hotfix SLA) and an enterprise-ready security questionnaire (SQ) template bundle for faster RFP responses. Primary goals: (1) quantify price elasticity across 1/2/3 year commits, (2) validate support-tiering that balances cost vs. emergency SLA needs, (3) create a prefilled SQ template and SOW language to reduce procurement friction for regulated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Run pilot quote for 4 enterprise prospects and record win/loss reasoning
Finalize price matrix for 1Y/2Y/3Y options with clear list prices and discount bands
Define three support tiers (Standard / Priority / Platinum) with documented SLAs and cost multipliers
Produce SQ template (SOC2, ISO references, KMS/HSM, network topology) and one completed customer-ready bundle
Define upgrade cadence policy and publishing cadence for release notes and opt-in rollouts
notes: Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report repeated procurement friction around upgrade cadence and emergency patching commitments for on-prem deals.

Tradeoffs considered: seat-based vs capacity-credit model. Initial pilot will price primarily as license fee + ops credits (capacity buffer) to preserve predictable revenue and align with Dedicated product economics.

Security posture: support for customer-managed KMS/HSM and on-prem audit logs is a gating factor for several prospects. SQ template must include answers and attachments for common questions (data flow diagrams, encryption-at-rest, patch window cadence, change management).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Created ticket after lead-gen call with three F500 prospects asking for guaranteed patching SLAs and fixed-price multi-year licensing. Initial ask: sample 3Y quote and emergency hotfix SLA.

2025-02-22 - Maya Chen: Ran a quick model to compare revenue and margin for seat vs license+ops credits. License+ops credits preserves unit economics with burst capacity. Recommendation: pilot license fee anchored to GPUs + ops credits for peak usage.

2025-02-26 - SolutionsEng (Anita Rao): Shared customer network diagram templates and noted that many customers require an on-prem upgrade blackout window during business hours. Proposed default non-invasive quarterly upgrade lane with opt-in monthly security patch lane for Platinum.

2025-03-01 - Legal (J. Morales): Provided redlines to SOW: need explicit rollback window and acceptance criteria for post-upgrade health checks. Asking PM to add change control appendix for on-prem upgrades.

2025-03-03 - Security (Rohan Patel): SQ draft added; flagged two high-risk items: (1) remote access for emergency hotfixes — must support customer-managed bastion and audit trails, (2) HSM integration detail missing for key wrap. Action: SolutionsEng to draft HSM integration note.

2025-03-05 - Maya Chen: Pricing matrix v0 posted to Drive (link above). Proposed list prices: 1Y = baseline, 2Y = baseline * 0.92, 3Y = baseline * 0.87 with minimum ops credit commitment equivalent to 20% of baseline monthly throughput. Feedback requested from sales by 2025-03-10.

2025-03-06 - Sales (E. Martinez): Ran two simulated quotes; Customer A (regulated fintech) accepted Platinum support & 3Y commit in internal mock. Customer B preferred 1Y with opt-in monthly patches. Suggest offering a limited-time 2% convert incentive for 2Y -> 3Y conversions.
decisions: Adopt license fee + ops credits pricing model for pilot (avoid seat complexity).
Support tiers to be: Standard (business-hours, 72h emergency), Priority (24/7, 48h emergency), Platinum (24/7, 24h emergency + on-call engineer).

Upgrade cadence defaults: quarterly automated non-breaking upgrades + opt-in monthly security patch lane for Priority/Platinum; emergency hotfix within SLA for Platinum with remote execution guardrails.
Produce a pre-filled SQ bundle and SOW appendix for legal/change control and HSM/KMS integration notes.
blockers: Finalize KMS/HSM integration note and internal security sign-off (owner: Rohan Patel).
Legal to approve SOW rollback/acceptance language (owner: J. Morales).
Sales to complete 4 live pilot quotes and share outcomes (owner: E. Martinez).

2025-03-10: Run pricing sensitivity session with Sales to validate discount bands and exportable quote templates.
2025-03-12: Security sign-off on SQ bundle; handoff to Legal for final SOW language.
2025-03-15: Collect pilot outcomes and decide whether to promote pricing model to ‘release candidate’ and include in private-2025.04 release notes.
